items.q: Uter pēs māior est, dexter an laevus?
items.en: Which of the two feet is bigger, the right or the left?
items.hint: an adjective in the nominative (agreeing with 'pēs')

items.en: What is the villa like?
Who is shouting and banging the door?
Where is Marcus's room?
Why is Marcus trying to break the door?
items.hint: a reason clause with 'quod' (he cannot ... otherwise)

items.q: Cūr Quīntus ē lectō surgere nōn potest?
items.en: Why can't Quintus get out of bed?
When were Quintus's feet equal?
What does Syra wonder at?
items.hint: an accusative with a perfect infinitive (that Quintus ...)

items.q: Quālia sunt ossa Quīntī, ut Syra dīcit?
items.en: What are Quintus's bones like, according to Syra?
items.hint: an adjective in the nominative neuter plural

items.en: Is Quintus crying?
Why is Quintus sad?
items.hint: a reason clause with 'quod' and 'necesse est' (he must ... inside)

items.en: Where does Syra sit down?

items.q: Num licet Mārcō cum puerīs lūdere?
items.en: Is Marcus allowed to play with the boys?

items.q: Cuius partis corporis dolōrēs Mārcus passus est?
items.en: Pains of which part of the body has Marcus suffered?
items.hint: a noun in the genitive (pains of the ...)

items.q: Quōmodo Mārcus hodiē in lūdum iit?
items.en: How did Marcus go to school today?

items.q: Cūr Mēdus heri domō fūgit, ut Syra putat?
items.en: Why did Medus run away from home yesterday, as Syra thinks?
items.hint: a reason clause with 'quia' and a perfect verb (he wanted to ...)

items.en: Where does Medus's girlfriend live?

items.q: Cui nihil difficile est, ut āiunt?
items.en: For whom is nothing difficult, as they say?
items.hint: a present participle in the dative (for one who ...)

items.en: Why was Marcus wet?
items.hint: a reason clause with 'quod' and a pluperfect verb (he had ...)

items.q: Cūr Mārcus sordidus atque cruentus erat?
items.en: Why was Marcus dirty and bloody?
items.hint: a reason clause with 'quod' and pluperfect verbs

items.en: Who had hit Marcus first?
How did the master scold Marcus?
Was the mother there when Marcus came back?

items.q: Quālis iam erat Mārcus, cum māter intrāvit?
items.en: What state was Marcus in by the time his mother came in?
items.hint: a perfect participle in the nominative (washed)

items.q: Num Mārcus sōlus in lūdō dormīverat?
items.en: Had Marcus been the only one asleep at school?
Who had written the beautiful letters?
How did Marcus lie?

items.q: Quōmodo Syra scit Sextum litterās scrīpsisse?
items.en: How does Syra know that Sextus wrote the letters?
items.hint: a reason with 'quia' and a pluperfect passive (the name had been ...)

items.en: Why did the letter-carrier shout?
items.hint: a reason with a perfect deponent verb (he feared ...)

items.en: What is the doorkeeper's dog like?
items.hint: a comparative adjective in the nominative (with 'lupō' in the ablative of comparison)

items.q: Num Quīntus umquam ā cane iānitōris morsus est?
items.en: Has Quintus ever been bitten by the doorkeeper's dog?
What did the letter-carrier bring?
items.hint: a noun in the accusative (the object)

items.en: What did Marcus finally admit?
items.hint: an accusative with a perfect infinitive, with 'sē' (that he had ...)

items.en: How many times had the master beaten Marcus?

items.q: Uter melior discipulus est, ut Quīntus dīcit, Quīntus an Mārcus?
items.en: Which of the two is the better pupil, according to Quintus, Quintus or Marcus?
Why was Quintus praised yesterday?
items.hint: a reason clause with 'quia' and pluperfect verbs (he had ... and had ...)

items.q: Quī laudātī sunt, ut Quīntus dīcit?
items.en: Who were praised, according to Quintus?
items.hint: a pronoun in the nominative with 'praeter' + accusative

items.q: Num Syra putat Mārcum Quīntō stultiōrem esse?
items.en: Does Syra think Marcus is more stupid than Quintus?

items.q: Quālis est Mārcus, ut Quīntus dīcit?
items.en: What is Marcus like, according to Quintus?
items.hint: a comparative adjective in the nominative (with 'nōbīs' in the ablative of comparison)
